data.title: A parser for TypeScript types, written in TypeScript types
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: "tsints" 是一个用 TypeScript 类型编写的 TypeScript 类型解析器，不包含任何 JavaScript 代码。它可以将 TypeScript 类型解析为类似 @babel/parser 生成的抽象语法树（AST）。项目提供了示例代码，展示如何使用 `Parse` 类型来解析特定字符串并生成相应的 AST。不过，由于其复杂的类型运算，每次运行 `tsc` 时可能会增加几秒的等待时间。项目目前有 17 个星标和一个分支，但尚未提供详细描述或发布任何版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript类型系统的复杂性和应用场景

不同观点：
• [正面观点] johnfn认为，尽管在工作中遇到TypeScript类型问题时可能会觉得无法解决，但想到有人能在TypeScript中实现像解析TypeScript类型这样复杂的任务，会感到自己的问题微不足道，从而受到激励去解决问题。drej补充了一个视频链接，展示如何在TypeScript类型系统中运行DOOM游戏，进一步强调这种复杂任务的可能性。

• [工具推荐] mpoteat提到一个工具（http://hkt.code.lol），为那些对TypeScript高级构建模块感兴趣的人提供类型级别的函数和解析器组合工具，基于高阶类型抽象。

• [比较观点] tmcanada提出TypeBox与mpoteat推荐的工具之间的比较，询问两者之间的差异。

• [质疑观点] nottorp质疑这种复杂的元编程是否必要，指出C++已经可以进行深度的元编程，并讽刺地问道是否能通过TypeScript类型系统在编译时运行整个工资应用。

• [技术背景] maxloh提供技术背景信息，指出TypeScript的类型系统是图灵完备的，并提供了一个相关GitHub问题的链接以供参考。

补充讨论：
• [批评观点] phplovesong认为TypeScript变得越来越像一种“ cult”（贬义），并表示TypeScript的理想状态是在2.x版本时，当时没有这些复杂的功能。每次听到Ocaml有复杂的类型系统时，他会提到TypeScript。

• [跑题与纠正] owebmaster调侃TypeScript像是一种“ cult”，而valenterry则表示自己发错了线程。

争议焦点：
• TypeScript类型系统的复杂性是否过度，以及这种复杂性是否真正有益于实际开发工作。Nottorp和phplovesong对这种复杂性持怀疑和批评态度，而johnfn和drej则认为这种复杂性展示了TypeScript的强大能力。

data.title: Rising young worker despair in the United States
data.author: johntfella
data.article_summary: 文章总结了美国年轻人工作者的精神绝望问题。从20世纪90年代初到2015年，精神绝望与年龄呈驼峰形关系：中年达到高峰，随后下降。然而，这种关系已发生变化，如今绝望感随年龄单调下降，主要由于年轻工作者绝望情绪的增加。不同劳动市场状态下，精神绝望与年龄的关系也有所不同：无法工作者和失业者仍呈现驼峰形关系，而家庭主妇、学生和退休人员的绝望感与年龄关系较为平坦。文章利用多个数据来源，如BRFSS（1993-2023）、NSDUH（2008-2023）等，证实了年轻工作者绝望上升的趋势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：年轻人面临的多重困境及其原因分析

不同观点：
• **年轻人面临多重压力**：[lordnacho]、[Zealotux]、[Havoc]等人认为，年轻人面临工作市场、住房市场、交友市场等多重压力。他们强调雇主通过技术加强对员工的控制，减少了员工的自主性，导致工作压力增加。此外，社会孤立、工会力量的减弱也让年轻人更难应对这些变化。[Havoc]具体列举了住房负担不起、工资低、社交媒体成瘾等一系列问题，认为这些问题比以往更加普遍和持久。

• **代际冲突和通货膨胀**：[thedevilslawyer]提出，高通胀可能是解决代际之间不公平负担的一种方式，认为老一辈可能在向新一代转嫁问题。

• **社会动荡和不平等**：[ipnon]指出，美国多数年轻人面临困境，导致社会动荡。同时，[Henchman21]将问题归咎于“婴儿潮”一代不愿让出权力和资源，进一步加剧了年轻人的困境。

• **技术和社会影响**：[jauntywundrkind]和[saubeidl]关注技术对社会的影响。[jauntywundrkind]认为现代技术让人们更加疏离，呼吁技术应更多地赋予人们自主权和尊严。[saubeidl]则从资本主义矛盾的角度分析，认为资本对利润的追求导致工人被剥削，最终可能引发系统性变革。

• **经济不平等和政策问题**：[bananapub]指出，年轻人感到必须通过不道德的手段（如诈骗、加密货币等）才能获得成功，这与当前政府的政策设置不当有关，比如过度保护老年人或富人，忽视年轻人的需求。

补充讨论：
• **数据和研究分析**：[GlibMonkeyDeath]对相关研究数据提出质疑，认为研究结果在某种程度上被过度简化。他指出，尽管年轻工人的“绝望”情绪有所增加，但大学教育程度的工人并没有显著变化。这一分析提示了不同群体间的差异。

• **消费主义和文化现象**：[Tycho]持不同观点，认为现代社会存在大量高收入工作和消费能力，指出人们在享受高消费娱乐活动，暗示年轻人的困境可能并非普遍存在。

争议焦点：
• **技术的作用和影响**：一些人认为技术加剧了年轻人的困境，尤其是通过监控和控制工作过程；另一些人则认为技术提供了更多高收入机会，关键在于如何看待和利用技术。

• **代际矛盾**：部分评论认为老一辈对资源和权力的掌控是年轻人困境的主要原因，而另一些人则关注经济结构性问题和社会动荡。

整体来看，评论主要围绕年轻人面临的经济、社会和心理压力展开，讨论了多重因素的交互影响，并提出了不同的解决思路和争议点。

Rising Young Worker Despair in the United States
David G. Blanchflower
&
Alex Bryson
Share
X
LinkedIn
Facebook
Bluesky
Threads
Email
Link
Working Paper
34071
DOI
10.3386/w34071
Issue Date
July 2025
Between the early 1990s and 2015 the relationship between mental despair and age was hump-shaped in the United States: it rose to middle-age, then declined later in life.  That relationship has now changed: mental despair declines monotonically with age due to a rise in despair among the young.  However, the relationship between age and mental despair differs by labor market status. The hump-shape in age still exists for those who are unable to work and the unemployed.  The relation between mental despair and age is broadly flat, and has remained so, for homemakers, students and the retired.  The change in the age-despair profile over time is due to increasing despair among young workers.  Whilst the relationship between mental despair and age has always been downward sloping among workers, this relationship has become more pronounced due to a rise in mental despair among young workers. We find broad-based evidence for this finding in the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) of 1993-2023, the National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH), 2008-2023, and in surveys by Pew, the Conference Board and Johns Hopkins University.

data.title: GHz spiking neuromorphic photonic chip with in-situ training
data.author: juanviera23
data.article_summary: 本文报道了一种千兆赫兹（GHz）光子尖峰神经形态芯片（PSNN），首次在互补金属氧化物半导体兼容的硅平台上实现了全栈大脑启发的计算。该芯片通过集成GHz非线性尖峰动态、现场学习能力、视网膜启发的编码方式，解决了时空数据整合和能效动态处理的长期挑战。实验显示，该光电神经形态系统在KTH视频识别数据集上达到了80%的准确率，处理速度比传统基于帧的方法快约100倍。该研究为低延迟、高吞吐量的光子神经形态计算铺平了道路，适用于实时动态视觉处理和自适应决策等高级应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于受启发于生物学的视频处理技术及其潜在应用和局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• [rf15] 认为尽管目前存在对大型语言模型（LLMs）的过度 hype，但仍然有人在进行类似于优化LLMs的工作。他提到在Hacker News（HN）上这种 hype 可能掩盖了其他重要内容。

• [vessenes] 强调了 GHz 速度视频处理的潜在应用价值，尤其是在大规模场景下的面部识别等任务。他认为即使只能进行基本的识别或分割，这种技术在军事和安全领域可能会有市场，并推动其商业化。

• [cwmoore] 对受视网膜启发的光处理技术表示赞赏，并期待未来可能出现类似视觉皮层的技术发展。

• [kadushka] 提出质疑，认为在构建硬件之前应先在软件中模拟算法。他指出，过去几十年中尝试让 spiking networks 工作一直未成功，如果软件中无法实现，硬件中也难以成功。

• [khalic] 对摘要中的不严谨声明表示不满，认为需要更多严格的论证和数据支持。

• [msgodel] 指出该技术目前仅使用了单层线性层，质疑其是否能实现更复杂的功能。他还提到如果理解正确的话，该技术在模型运行时无法直接使用，需要以传统方式记录和处理权重。

Abstract:
Neuromorphic photonic computing represents a paradigm shift for next-generation machine intelligence, yet critical gaps persist in emulating the brain's event-driven, asynchronous dynamics,a fundamental barrier to unlocking its full potential. Here, we report a milestone advancement of a photonic spiking neural network (PSNN) chip, the first to achieve full-stack brain-inspired computing on a complementary metal oxide semiconductor-compatible silicon platform. The PSNN features transformative innovations of gigahertz-scale nonlinear spiking dynamics,in situ learning capacity with supervised synaptic plasticity, and informative event representations with retina-inspired spike encoding, resolving the long-standing challenges in spatiotemporal data integration and energy-efficient dynamic processing. By leveraging its frame-free, event-driven working manner,the neuromorphic optoelectronic system achieves 80% accuracy on the KTH video recognition dataset while operating at ~100x faster processing speeds than conventional frame-based approaches. This work represents a leap for neuromorphic computing in a scalable photonic platform with low latency and high throughput, paving the way for advanced applications in real-time dynamic vision processing and adaptive decision-making, such as autonomous vehicles and robotic navigation.

data.title: Palantir is extending its reach even further into government
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary:
特朗普政府大幅增加了与Palantir的合作，使这家由其盟友彼得·蒂尔共同创办的公司成为政府首选软件开发商。在终止与埃森哲、博思艾伦和德勤等咨询巨头和政府承包商的巨额合同后，Palantir脱颖而出，不仅获得了超过1.13亿美元的联邦支出，还与被终止合同的公司合作，为它们提供支持，同时巩固自身影响力。

Palantir的软件已成为政府系统的核心工具，例如与国税局合作开发“大API”以统一数据，以及与移民和海关执法局签订3000万美元合同追踪自遣返。五角大楼也授予Palantir一份7.95亿美元的合同，扩展其Maven智能系统项目，总合同上限达13亿美元。

尽管其他公司失去数十亿美元的政府合同，Palantir却通过与这些公司合作，加速其软件和AI技术在联邦政府的应用。例如，与埃森哲合作培训员工使用其Foundry软件和AI技术，以提升政府效率。

白宫对与Palantir的合作表示赞赏，称其为高标准的美国公司，有助于提高政府效率。

President Donald Trump’s
administration has dramatically expanded its work with Palantir, elevating the company cofounded by Trump ally Peter Thiel as the government’s go-to software developer. Following massive contract terminations for consulting giants and government contractors like Accenture, Booz Allen, and Deloitte, Palantir has emerged ahead. Now the data analytics firm is partnering with those companies—offering them a lifeline while consolidating its own power.
Palantir has become one of the few winners in the Trump administration’s cost-cutting efforts,
receiving more than $113 million
in federal spending since the beginning of the year, according to The New York Times. Palantir’s US government revenue has grown by more than $ 370 million compared to this time last year, according to the company’s
most recent quarterly earnings report
. Before making remarks at last week’s AI Summit in DC, Trump thanked a variety of cabinet secretaries and tech leaders,
including Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar
. “We buy a lot of things from Palantir,” Trump said. “Are we paying our bills? I think so.”
Instead of replacing these more traditional contractors, Palantir’s software is becoming the core tool deployed by them in government systems, placing Palantir in a newly central role.
The White House itself is thrilled by this partnership: “The Trump Administration has high-standard [sic] when spending American’s hard-earned tax dollars—which is why agencies have partnered with Palantir, a top-tier American company renowned for their longstanding history of innovation, results, and increasing government efficiency,” says White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers.
Palantir did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
In April,
WIRED reported that Palantir was working alongside IRS engineers
to build what sources called a “mega API,” which would unify all data across the agency. An API, or application programming interface, enables applications and databases to exchange data and possibly compare it against other interoperable datasets. Once completed, this mega API could become the “read center of all IRS systems.” Immigration and Customs Enforcement
contracted Palantir for $30 million
to track self-deportations in April. The company has also won federal contracts more recently, like a $795 million award from the Pentagon in May to expand its Maven Smart System program. The total contract ceiling for the Army’s Maven program is now $1.3 billion.
This growth comes as some of the companies Palantir has chosen to partner with have lost billions in government contract cuts. In April, defense secretary Pete Hegseth announced plans to cut $5.1 billion in IT consulting contracts with companies including Accenture, Booz Allen, and Deloitte.
In a memo announcing the cuts
, Hegseth said that the Pentagon would be forced to bring more of its IT work in-house.
“These contracts represent non-essential spending on third party consultants to perform services more efficiently performed by the highly skilled members of our DoD workforce using existing resources,” Hegseth wrote.
Palantir’s partnerships with these companies vary, but each one makes it easier for Palantir to extend the reach of its software and AI technology across the federal government. With Accenture’s government branch, Palantir will train and certify at least 1,000 Accenture workers on its Foundry software as well as its AI tech,
according to an Accenture press release
The companies also said that together they could create “a 360-degree view” of government agency budgets, something the so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) has sought to build and use to review federal spending. (Palantir
partnered with Accenture before in 2022
, but this is the first partnership to focus on US government clients.)
“We are teaming up with Accenture Federal Services to accelerate AI across the U.S. Government, working to address federal agencies’ highest-priority operational challenges,” Palantir posted to X last month.
"What makes this partnership so uniquely powerful is Accenture’s expertise working with the federal government and our ability to bring commercial capabilities to government solutions, combined with Palantir’s deep experience in government software," Julie Sweet, chair and CEO of Accenture, said in a press release. “Together, we will harness the ever-growing power of AI to help the federal government succeed in its critical mission to modernize and reinvent its operations—with stronger data flows, transparency and resilience—to better serve warfighters, citizens and all its stakeholders.”
Accenture did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: A deep dive into Rust and C memory interoperability
data.author: hyperbrainer
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了Rust和C语言内存分配器交互时可能出现的问题，特别是内存管理中的危险和误区。作者通过一次面试问题引发的思考，深入研究了为何不应混合使用不同语言的内存分配器。文章详细解释了退出代码在内存测试中的意义，强调了内存损坏但未被检测出的危险性（退出代码0），因为这可能导致程序在后续运行中出现不可预知的问题。

作者逐步构建了一个内存测试环境，通过一系列实验展示了不同内存分配策略的结果，揭示了内存访问的实际成本、堆的管理以及CPU缓存对性能的影响。文章最后总结了关键要点，提醒开发者在处理内存管理时需格外小心，并提供了调试建议和实验重现方法。

本文适合有一定Rust和C编程基础，并希望深入了解内存管理的读者。

主要讨论点：Rust与C语言内存分配与释放的兼容性问题，以及对某篇文章的质量和生成方式的讨论。

不同观点：
• [veber-alex] 认为Rust默认使用libc分配器，因此在Rust中分配内存而在C中释放（或反之）不会导致崩溃。他提供了相关文档链接以支持其观点。
• [mwkaufma] 认为该评论内容详尽但实质内容少，且标题有误导性，甚至怀疑内容是由GPT生成的。
• [eatonphil] 关注将Rust代码集成到Postgres中的问题，尤其是涉及到Postgres自有分配器系统时，期待Rust标准库支持传递分配器以简化复杂数据结构的处理。
• [phkahler] 关心如何在C和Rust之间共享结构体，尤其是通过访问函数还是直接访问成员，并请求相关文档或博客的指引。
• [commandersaki] 对通过FFI调用时内存分配和释放的细节感到困惑，特别是关于调用libc free和Rust dealloc的区别。
• [7e] 强烈反对用C分配内存而在Rust中释放的做法，认为这种期望是不合理的，建议Rust通过回调让C来释放内存。

补充讨论：
• [tracker1] 认为该文章对于混合代码库的开发者来说是有价值的知识基础。
• [sesm] 指出文章中缺少声称包含的面试问题。

• [jokoon] 突然插入，询问有关付费Rust工作机会的问题，与主要讨论点无关。
• [Tony_Delco] 赞赏文章的写作风格，认为对内存分配危险的深入探讨很有价值，即便文章是由AI生成的。

• 文章内容的真实性和可信度，尤其是其是否由GPT生成以及是否值得阅读。
• Rust与C之间内存分配和释放的兼容性及其实践方法。

Part 1: A Deep Dive into Rust and C Memory Interoperability
An in-depth exploration of what happens when Rust and C memory allocators collide, featuring crash analysis.
views
|
comments
“Memory oppresses me.” - Severian, The Book of the New Sun
Interviewer
: “What happens if you allocate memory with C’s malloc and try to free it with Rust’s dealloc, if you get a pointer to the memory from C?”
Me
: “If we do it via FFI then there’s a possibility the program may continue working (because the underlying structs share the same memory layout? right? …right?)”
Now if you have any experience working with memory management, you know that this is a dangerous answer. But I didn’t know it at the time. I was just trying to get through the interview.
But I realized at that moment that I had been treating memory allocators like black boxes. I knew the rules - never mix allocators - but I didn’t truly understand
why
. So here’s my attempt at de-mystifying memory management, starting with the fundamentals and building a testing laboratory to explore what happens when different memory worlds collide.
Prerequisites
#
To get the most from this article, you should be familiar with:
Basic Rust and C programming
Pointers and memory management concepts
Command line tools (bash, gcc, cargo)
Basic understanding of stack vs heap
Don’t worry if you’re not an expert, I’m not one either - but I’ll explain concepts as best I can!
Table of Contents
#
The Interview Question That Started Everything
Why Memory Allocators Don’t Mix
Memory Fundamentals: Building Our Mental Model
Building a Memory Testing Laboratory
First Experiments: Surprising Results
Key Takeaways and What’s Next
The Interview Question That Started Everything
#
It was Friday afternoon when I had an interview for an amazing startup which focuses on building very high performance systems. The interview experience was intense while being highly rewarding. We touched upon topics async runtimes, memory management, rust FFI etc.
The intention wasn’t to test my language specific knowledge but being able to reason about how these systems work at a level closer to the machine.
It caught me a little offguard. It’s not something I had prepared for. However, to be a good systems engineer, It is essential to develop a knack for the fundamentals - understanding how things work all the way down to the metal. Whether it’s the intricacies of the CPU cache hierarchy, memory alignment, or the behavior of allocators under concurrency, these low-level details can have profound impacts on system performance and correctness.
That experience prompted me to reflect on my own gaps and sparked a sort of yearning to dig deeper into the topic. Hence, I decided to do this and start a journey to understand memory management better, starting with the basics and building a comprehensive testing framework to explore the interactions between Rust and C memory allocators.
Why Memory Allocators Don’t Mix
#
Before diving into the technical details, let’s understand the fundamental problem. But first, we need to establish what different exit codes mean when testing memory operations:
Understanding Exit Codes in Memory Testing
#
When experimenting with memory allocators, the exit code tells us exactly what happened:
Exit Code
Signal
Meaning
Safety
0
None
Process completed “successfully”
⚠️
DANGEROUS
- Silent corruption
-11 or 139
SIGSEGV
Segmentation fault - invalid memory access
✅ Safe - OS detected bad access
-6 or 134
SIGABRT
Program aborted - allocator detected corruption
✅ Safe - Allocator safety checks worked
⚠️
The Hidden Danger of Exit Code 0
When mixing allocators, exit code 0 is the worst possible outcome. It means memory corruption occurred but went undetected. Your program continues running with a corrupted heap - a time bomb that will explode unpredictably later. A crash (SIGSEGV or SIGABRT) is actually the safe outcome because it prevents further corruption.
Now, when you write:
// dangerous.rs
let
ptr
=
unsafe
{
libc
::
malloc
(
64
) };
rust

作者逐步构建了一个内存测试环境，通过一系列实验展示了不同内存分配策略的结果，揭示了内存访问的实际成本、堆的管理以及CPU缓存对性能的影响。文章最后总结了关键要点，提醒开发者在处理内存管理时需格外小心，并提供了调试建议和实验重现方法。

本文适合有一定Rust和C编程基础，并希望深入了解内存管理的读者。

data.title: My Ideal Array Language
data.author: bobajeff
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了理想数组语言应具备的特性，以适应现代异构硬件的发展。作者强调，随着更多核心、更多种类的子系统（如GPU、FPGA）以及更复杂的计算单元的出现，编程语言必须能够有效利用这些资源。理想的数组语言应具备用户可扩展的秩多态性（Rank Polymorphism），如Numpy和JAX虽然提供了一些支持，但需要结合JIT编译器和内核语言才能完全实现数组语言的功能。作者还提到Mojo语言的用户可扩展性以及MLIR原语在其中的作用。此外，文章指出，数组语言应具备值语义和自动缓冲化，以帮助编译器生成更高效的代码，类似于Fortran编译器的优化能力。最终，作者认为无法适应硬件发展趋势的语言和编译器将逐渐被淘汰。

44785224.article_content:
My Ideal Array Language
2025-07-20
What do I think the ideal array language should look like?
My Ideal Array Language
Why does this matter?
User-Extensible Rank Polymorphism
User Extensibility in Mojo
Value Semantics and Automatic Bufferization
Fortran’s Array Semantics
Comparison with MLIR Types and Concepts
Fortran Array Semantics in MLIR
Aside: Dependent Types in Fortran
Compilation Step
Offline vs Online Compilation
Compiler Transparency and Inspectability
Example: NVHPC’s User-Facing Optimization Reporting
SIMT and Automatic Parallelization
SIMT vs SIMD
Default Modes of Parallelism
Array-Aware Type System
Syntax
Conclusion
Bonus:
Comparing Parallel Functional Array Languages
Why does this matter?
The fundamental units of computation available to users today are not the same as they were 20 years ago.
When users had at most a few cores on a single CPU, it made complete sense that every program was written with the assumption that it would only run on a single core.
Even in a high-performance computing (HPC) context, the default mode of parallelism was (for a long time) the Message Passing Interface (MPI), which is a
descriptive
model of multi-core and multi-node parallelism.
Most code was still basically written with the same assumtions: all units of computation were assumed to be uniform.
Hardware has trended towards heterogeneity in several ways:
More cores per node
More nodes per system
More kinds of subsystems (GPUs, FPGAs, etc.)
More kinds of computational units on a single subsystem
CPUs have lots of vector units and specialized instructions
NVIDIA GPUs have lots of tensor cores specialized for matrix operations
New paradigms at the assembly level
Scalable Vector Extensions (SVE) and Scalable Matrix Extensions (SMEs) on Arm
Tight hardware release schedules, meaning less and less time in between changes in hardware and more and more rewrites required for hand-written code at the lowest level
The old assumptions do not hold true anymore, and programming languages need to be aware of these changes and able to optimize around them.
Imagine the units of computation available in 2025 as a spectrum from SIMD units, to tensor cores, to CUDA cores, to small power-efficient Arm CPU cores, to large beefy AMD CPUs.
It is easy to imagine this spectrum filling in with more specialized hardware pushing the upper and lower boundaries and filling in the gaps.
One day it might be as natural to share work between nodes as it is between individual SIMD lanes on a single CPU core.
This level of heterogeneity is not something that can be ignored by a programming language or a programming language ecosystem.
I believe languages and compilers that do not consider the trajectory of hardware development will be left behind to some degree.
User-Extensible Rank Polymorphism
IMO this is what makes something an array language.
No language can be an array language without rank polymorphism.
Numpy provides
some
rank polymorphism, but it’s not a first-class
language
feature.
Numpy also needs to be paired with a JIT compiler to make python a real array language, so NUMBA or another kernel language is required for Python to make the list.
Otherwise, users would not be able to write their own polymorphic kernels (
ufunc
s).
Similarly, the JAX and XLA compilers provide an array language base, but without a kernel language like Pallas or Triton, it’s not extensible enough for every use case they care about.
A proper array language will have an array language
base
with the ability to write
kernels
directly, either by exposing lower-level details the user can opt-in to, or by allowing primitives to be composed in a way the compiler can reason about.
User Extensibility in Mojo
TODO: unfinished section
MLIR primitives exposed in the language
Pushing details out of the compiler and into the language
Helps extensibility; fewer uses of compiler builtins
Standard library contains lots of language features that are usually implemented in the compiler
recent talk on
GPUMODE
Value Semantics and Automatic Bufferization
Most of the major ML frameworks have value semantics for arrays by default, and it gives the compiler much more leeway when it comes to memory.
Not only is manual memory management a huge pain and a source of bugs, if the ownership semantics are not sufficiently represented in the language or the language defaults are not ammenable to optimization, the compiler will have a much harder time generating performant code.
My understanding of the Rust borrow checker is that its purpose is to handle the intersection of manual memory management and strict ownership.
Users choose between value and reference semantics, and the compiler helps you keep track of ownership.
Summarized as
“aliasing xor mutability”
.
Thanks Steve, for helping clarify the Rust bits!
Fortran’s Array Semantics
In a way, value semantics and automatic bufferization of arrays is part of why Fortran compilers are able to generate such performant code.

data.title: Century-old stone “tsunami stones” dot Japan's coastline (2015)
data.author: deegles
data.article_summary: 在日本东北部沿海的小村庄Aneyoshi，一块刻有警示的“海啸石”提醒村民不要在标记以下建造房屋，以避免海啸灾难。这些石头是祖先为了警示后代在遭遇地震后应前往高处避难而设立的，许多石头可以追溯到1896年两次致命海啸之后。然而，随着沿海城镇的发展和防波堤的建设，这些警告逐渐被遗忘。不过，在Aneyoshi等一些地方，居民仍然遵循石碑的警示。2011年东日本大地震和海啸后，部分地区仍在恢复中，约23万人仍住在临时住房中，海啸还导致了福岛第一核电站事故。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"海啸石"（Tsunami Stones）的历史、意义及其现代启示的讨论。

不同观点：
• teleforce：提到福岛第一核电站建在海啸石警告线之外，暗示古人对自然灾害有预见。如果立石的人还在世，他们会有一种“我早就告诉过你”的感受。
• atopal：联想到德国的“饥饿石”，它们具有类似的警示作用，提醒后人自然灾害的影响。
• willidiots：通过1700年卡斯卡迪亚俯冲带地震的例子，指出古代海啸记录对现代科学研究的重要性。
• rembal：认为有关海啸石的文章像海啸石本身一样，每隔几年就会出现在公众视野中，显示出集体记忆的周期性。
• xrayarx：引用了纽约时报的文章，提供有关海啸石的进一步阅读材料。
• burnt-resistor：建议在容易发生山洪的地区设立类似海啸石的警示标志，例如塔加上铭文和风向袋。
• NaOH：提到以前关于海啸石的讨论和文章，提供相关链接和评论数量，显示出这个话题的长期关注度。
• porphyra：指出1896年的海啸石其实并不算非常古老，认为它们只有上千年的历史。
• josefritzishere：提供更详细的信息，指出在日本有317块海啸石，其中125块在2011年海啸中被摧毁，显示出这些石碑的脆弱性。
• anonu：联想到黎巴嫩山中的罗马时代石刻，强调古代就有自然保护的意识。
• Mistletoe：对长期思考表示兴趣，提问现代人应该留下什么样的“海啸石”来警示后代，以防止未来灾难。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个历史和地理背景的例子，如福岛核电站、德国饥饿石、黎巴嫩的罗马石刻等，显示出不同文化和地区对自然灾害的相似应对策略。
• 争议焦点可能在于海啸石的实际效果和现代社会的记忆周期。一些人认为这些石碑的警示作用有限，因为集体记忆周期较短，而另一些人则认为它们具有重要的历史和教育意义。
• 还有人思考现代社会应该如何留下类似的长期警示，以防止未来灾难，这涉及到对当前和未来社会的深刻思考。

44785107.article_content:
T.KISHIMOTO, via Wikimedia Commons.
At the edge of Aneyoshi, a small village on Japan’s northeastern coast, a 10-foot-tall stone tablet stands, carved with a dire warning to locals.
"High dwellings are the peace and harmony of our descendants," the rock slab says. "Remember the calamity of the great tsunamis. Do not build any homes below this point."
While the Aneyoshi tablet might be the most straightforward, so-called “tsunami stones” dot Japan’s coastline, warning the carvers’ descendants to seek high ground after earthquakes in case they foreshadow destructive waves. The stones vary in degrees of repair, with most dating back to around 1896, when two deadly tsunamis killed about 22,000 people,
Martin Fackler writes for
The New York Times
.
“The tsunami stones are warnings across generations, telling descendants to avoid the same suffering of their ancestors,” Itoko Kitahara, a historian of natural disasters at Ritsumeikan University in Kyoto,
told Fackler in 2011
after an earthquake killed nearly 29,000 people.
“Some places heeded these lessons of the past, but many didn’t,” Kitahara
told Fackler
.
Over the decades, the stones’ warnings were disregarded or forgotten by many as coastal towns boomed and people placed their faith in massive seawalls built by the Japanese government. But in some places like Aneyoshi, residents still heeded the tsunami stones’ warnings.
"Everybody here knows about the markers. We studied them in school," 12-year-old Yuto Kimura told
the Associated Press in 2011
. "When the tsunami came, my mom got me from school and then the whole village climbed to higher ground."
Aneyoshi’s tsunami stone is the only one found that explicitly describes where to build houses, but centuries of tsunamis have also left their marks on the names of places in the region,
Fackler writes
. While some places have names like “Valley of the Survivors” and “Wave’s Edge” that might indicate ground high enough to escape a massive wave, places that weren’t so lucky might instead be named “Octopus Grounds,” after the sea life left behind in the rubble.
"It takes about three generations for people to forget. Those that experience the disaster themselves pass it to their children and their grandchildren, but then the memory fades," Fumihiko Imamura, a professor in disaster planning at Tohoku University,
told the AP
.
Four years later,
parts of Japan are still recovering
from the March 2011 tsunami, with about 230,000 people still living in temporary housing. The tsunami and accompanying earthquake were also responsible for the Fukushima Daiichi disaster, when equipment damaged during the  disaster triggered a nuclear meltdown

• burnt-resistor：建议在容易发生山洪的地区设立类似海啸石的警示标志，例如塔加上铭文和风向袋。
• NaOH：提到以前关于海啸石的讨论和文章，提供相关链接和评论数量，显示出这个话题的长期关注度。
• porphyra：指出1896年的海啸石其实并不算非常古老，认为它们只有上千年的历史。
• josefritzishere：提供更详细的信息，指出在日本有317块海啸石，其中125块在2011年海啸中被摧毁，显示出这些石碑的脆弱性。
• anonu：联想到黎巴嫩山中的罗马时代石刻，强调古代就有自然保护的意识。
• Mistletoe：对长期思考表示兴趣，提问现代人应该留下什么样的“海啸石”来警示后代，以防止未来灾难。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个历史和地理背景的例子，如福岛核电站、德国饥饿石、黎巴嫩的罗马石刻等，显示出不同文化和地区对自然灾害的相似应对策略。
• 争议焦点可能在于海啸石的实际效果和现代社会的记忆周期。一些人认为这些石碑的警示作用有限，因为集体记忆周期较短，而另一些人则认为它们具有重要的历史和教育意义。
• 还有人思考现代社会应该如何留下类似的长期警示，以防止未来灾难，这涉及到对当前和未来社会的深刻思考。

data.title: Scientists shine a laser through a human head
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 科学家们通过将激光照射穿过人头，成功追踪了光子路径，这是开发廉价新型医学成像仪的第一步。由格拉斯哥大学的Extreme Light小组进行的研究展示了利用光子进行脑成像的潜力。传统成像技术昂贵且复杂，而这种新方法利用激光和探测器，通过追踪穿过头部的少量光子，可能带来更经济、简便的成像解决方案，未来或可应用于医学诊断领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过激光测量光子穿过人脑的实验及其相关技术和安全问题

不同观点：
• **对实验的安全性和可行性表示乐观**：
  - [hollerith] 提到实验使用800纳米波长的光，而阳光中包含大量该波长的光，因此认为该实验可能是完全无害的。
  
• **对实验设置和技术的质疑**：
  - [bbor] 对IEEE的报道框架提出质疑，认为大脑皮层（外层）才是主要研究对象，而跨头设置的发射器-探测器布局难以区分多个发射器的信号，无法有效映射氧合水平。同时指出fNIRS和EEG依赖复杂的统计方法来构建3D活动模型，质疑如何通过单一设置实现有效测量。
  
• **提及相关领域的前沿研究**：
  - [bbor] 还提到频率调制在fNIRS设置中的前沿研究，认为复杂性极高，但也暗示可能低估了现有工具的能力。

• **对具体技术问题的关注**：
  - [Onavo] 提出深色头发对fNIR系统的影响仍然是一个主要问题，质疑该问题是否得到解决。
  
• **对实验的幽默或讽刺评论**：
  - [pixelpoet] 以幽默的方式提到Cornell box路径追踪问题。
  - [luguenth] 开玩笑说锡箔帽有了实际应用。
  - [cadr] 以幽默方式警告不要用剩下的眼睛看激光。

• **对未来科技发展的期望和伦理问题**：
  - [echelon] 认为应该有办法非侵入性地获取高空间和时间分辨率的信号，以重建人们的思维、记忆和感觉，并呼吁继续推动这些边界。

补充讨论：
• **关联历史事件**：
  - [HelloUsername] 提到Anatoli Bugorski事件，一位苏联科学家在1978年幸存于高能质子束穿过头部的事故，以此来对比和引发讨论。

• **提供资源和工具推荐**：
  - [bbor] 提供了关于fNIRS和EEG的资源链接，并推荐了Unicorn EEG系统，鼓励黑客社区参与这些领域的研究。

争议焦点：
• **实验设置的有效性和信号解析能力**：[bbor] 对跨头发射器-探测器设置的有效性提出质疑，特别是如何区分多个信号源并映射大脑氧合水平的问题，这与其他评论中对实验安全性和技术进步的乐观态度形成对比。

data.title: Do LLMs identify fonts?
data.author: alexmolas
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一个用于识别字体的网站dafont.com，该网站拥有比Google Fonts更全面和独特的字体库。作者特别提到网站论坛中一个长期未被解答的字体识别请求，并由此引发了一个实验：使用大型语言模型（LLM）来自动识别字体。为了确保评估的公正性，作者仅让LLM识别未被社区识别的字体，并通过与社区答案对比来评估LLM的表现。作者实施了一个实时基准测试，涉及两个LLM模型（gpt-4o-mini和gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20），并允许每个模型最多猜测五次，使用top-$k$准确度指标进行评估。实验结果显示LLM的表现不佳，作者认为这可能是因为任务难度高或模型未见过这些图像。文章最后提到相关Python脚本和工具，如Simon Willison的llm包和GitHub Actions工作流，所有结果存储在JSON文件中，并通过GitHub Pages托管实时基准测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用OCR和LLMs进行字体识别和文档处理的有效性及技术细节

不同观点：
• StellarScience认为Microsoft Word在离线状态下依然可以很好地进行OCR并匹配字体，表明其使用的是传统OCR算法而非LLMs。他们强调LLMs只是工具之一，并非万能。
• elicash期待LLMs未来不仅能识别字体，还能通过分析上下文和删除部分的长度来解密文档中被涂黑的部分。
• she46BiOmUerPVj提到使用"What The Font"工具来进行字体识别，而不是依赖LLMs。
• Rastonbury的经验表明LLMs在建议类似字体方面表现尚可，至少对于未经训练的眼睛来说足够接近。
• larodi质疑是否真的需要在训练集中包含字体信息，认为只需将字符解释为特定字母即可，无需提供字体名称。
• Doohickey-d好奇更昂贵的LLMs（如GPT-4）是否会有更好的表现，认为所选的LLMs可能并非最优秀的。
• Workaccount2提出广告中的字体可能只是一次性绘制的，而非使用现有字体。
• cormullion怀疑专业广告中使用的字体不太可能来自dafont.com，并且字体识别程序通常是基于商业可用字体进行训练的。
• gdudeman指出实验方法中缺少关于是否开启思考模式、是否允许网络搜索和工具使用的信息，并认为LLMs可能通过推理得出字体。
• micromacrofoot提到错误猜测的字体有多接近，指出由于字体形状无法版权保护，导致很多相似字体存在，尤其是在免费网站上。
• mopsi分享了使用各种工具（包括LLMs和WhatTheFont）进行字体识别的经验，最终通过ChatGPT的文本描述找到正确字体。
• HocusLocus认为直接询问文档创建者是最简单的方法，质疑使用大量能源进行模拟的过程，强调资源消耗问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了传统OCR算法与LLMs在字体识别中的作用和局限性。
• 有人期待LLMs未来在文档处理和字体识别方面有更多功能，如解密涂黑部分。
• 关于字体识别工具的讨论，如"What The Font"，以及这些工具与LLMs的比较。
• 对LLMs在字体识别中的实际表现存在不同看法，有人认为表现尚可，有人认为不够准确。
• 资源消耗和环保问题也被提及，作为对依赖数据中心进行复杂计算的批评。

44746347.article_content:
Spoiler:
not really
dafont.com
is a wonderful website that contains a large collection of fonts. It’s more comprehensive and esoteric than Google Fonts. One of its features is a forum where users can ask for help identifying fonts – check out
this poor fellow
who’s been waiting for over two years and bumped his thread. I thought it would be interesting to see if an LLM could do this task, so I scraped the forum and set up a benchmark.
I implemented this as a live benchmark. By this I mean that I only ask the LLMs to identify fonts that haven’t yet been identified by the community. I evaluate the LLMs prediction by comparing it to the community’s prediction, once the latter has been made. This way, I’m sure that I’m asking the LLM to work on images it has never seen before. Indeed, there are many examples of biased LLMs that are just too good at memorizing
images
and
text
.
Benchmark contamination is a real issue in LLM evaluation, so I think it’s important to set up benchmarks this way when possible. There have been some great suggestions in this direction, including
LiveBench
and the
Konwinski Prize
I evaluated only two LLMs:
gpt-4o-mini
and
gemini-2.5-flash-preview-05-20
. Each LLM is provided with the image uploaded by the user, the title of the thread, and a description if there is one. Providing these last two pieces of context is important, because some images contain several fonts, and the title or description may help the LLM focus on the right one. Take for instance this Marmite image:
Here are a couple extra difficult cases:
Each LLM is allowed to make up to five guesses. This allows calculating the accuracy at different levels of leniency. The performance is thus measured with a top-$k$ accuracy metric, which considers the LLM’s first $k$ guesses and checks if the correct font is among them. I ran this benchmark for a few weeks, and here are the results as of writing this recap:
I find these results quite abysmal. It’s hard to tell whether this is because the task is too difficult, or because the LLMs is being fairly evaluated on images it’s never seen before. Answering this question would require going deeper and evaluating the LLMs on old images which it may have already seen. Anyway, I’m happy in a weird way to have found a classification task which LLMs are not good at (yet?). I think this is a good reminder that LLMs are not magic, and that they still have a long way to go before being able to solve all tasks.
Implementation notes
There’s a Python script for
scraping dafont.com
, and another one for
prompting
the LLMs. It’s the first I picked
uv
and it was a great experience. There’s a simple
GitHub Actions workflow
which runs every 3 hours. The LLM logic is written with
Simon Willison’s llm
package, which is super straightforward. All the results are stored in JSON files, and the benchmark is made with
Observable Framework
. I had been meaning to try it for a while, and I have to say it’s nice to define a dashboard with source code instead of a GUI. The live benchmark is hosted with GitHub Pages
here
.

data.title: OpenIPC: Open IP Camera Firmware
data.author: zakki
data.article_summary: OpenIPC是一个开源的IP摄像头固件，旨在替代厂商预装的封闭、不安全且常被弃更的固件。它支持ARM和MIPS处理器，提供预编译二进制文件和完整源代码，采用MIT许可证，允许代码重用于任何目的，包括专有软件。OpenIPC提供自由和安全性，用户可完全控制摄像头，避免后门和恶意软件。它支持多种摄像头，基础功能包括视频和音频流。此外，还支持外部云存储、YouTube和Telegram流媒体、SOCKS5代理、虚拟隧道等功能。另有针对无人机、安全头盔、医疗研究等特殊设备的版本。使用OpenIPC于军事目的不被允许，商业使用需联系项目方。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IP摄像头的选择，特别是开源支持和可靠性方面的讨论

不同观点：
• miiiiiike 认为选择IP摄像头时品牌和可靠性让人困惑，寻求具备良好开源支持且可靠的品牌，特别是需要支持PoE的室内外摄像头。
• cnst 推荐了Wansview Q5和Cinnado D1 2k等价格较低且有开源支持的摄像头，提供了具体的购买链接和价格信息。
• roacato 指出OpenIPC的主录制/编码应用（majestic）并非完全开源，推荐了thingino作为全开源的替代方案。
• KyleBerezin 认为支持硬件的列表主要针对SoC，而不是品牌，这使得确定具备所需芯片的物理摄像头变得困难，且大部分支持的设备似乎是网络摄像头，而非现代现成的IP摄像头。
• jtchang 分享了自己对Wyze Cam V2进行逆向工程并制作自定义固件的经验，强调了制作长期可支持的开源摄像头软件/固件的难度，并指出即使开源固件也并非完全开源。
• MostlyStable 推荐了FOSCAM 3k wifi摄像头，支持RTSP流标准和CGIProxy命令，可以在不使用官方应用和云服务的情况下实现本地集成。

44758463.article_content:
OpenIPC is an alternative open firmware for your IP camera.
OpenIPC is an open source operating system from the open community targeting for IP cameras with ARM and MIPS processors from several manufacturers in order to replace that closed, opaque, insecure, often abandoned and unsupported firmware pre-installed by a vendor.
OpenIPC Firmware comes as binary pre-compiled files for easy installation by end-user. Also, we provide full access to the source files for further development and improvement by any capable programmer willing to contribute to the project. OpenIPC source code is released under one of the most simple open source license agreements,
MIT License
, giving users express permission to reuse code for any purpose, even as part of a proprietary software. We only ask you politely to contribute your improvements back to us and also be sure to contact us if you use our project for
commercial purposes
. We would be grateful for any feedback and suggestions. The use of the OpenIPC project and its components for military purposes is not permitted.
Installation Instructions
Precompiled binary files
Source code on GitHub
OpenIPC Firmware uses
Buildroot
to build its Linux distro, and utilizes either
Majestic
,
Divinus
,
Mini
or
Venc
streamer.
Majestic code while is not open, provides unprecedented performance and capabilities for a wide range of hardware. The author of Majestic streamer is looking into possibilities to open-source the codebase after he secures enough funds to support further open development. You can
help
to make it happen sooner.
Why OpenIPC Firmware?
First of all, OpenIPC Firmware brings you freedom. With OpenIPC on your camera you are the master of your streams. You have full access to the system and can control what, where, and how you want your camera to behave. There are no backdoors, no botnets, no crypto-mining malware, no keyloggers, no password sniffers, nothing you could possibly expect in a closed binary system with no access to its source code.
As for the Firmware capabilities, we strive to provide universal support for a wide range of cameras, thus we are focused on basic functionality first, allowing end-users to upgrade their cameras' firmware and stream video and audio (where supported) without too much hassle.
We have some interesting bits though. Our Firmware supports external IPEYE cloud storage, streaming video to Youtube and Telegram, using SOCKS5 proxy, setting up a Virtual Tunnel, and more.
There are also several projects focused on specialized equipment, such as a camera to be mounted on a drone, for mounting on construction helmets, for use in surveying tools, for medical research of the organs of vision, underwater fishing, etc.
Alliance
Supporters
44758463.article_summary: OpenIPC是一个开源的IP摄像头固件，旨在替代厂商预装的封闭、不安全且常被弃更的固件。它支持ARM和MIPS处理器，提供预编译二进制文件和完整源代码，采用MIT许可证，允许代码重用于任何目的，包括专有软件。OpenIPC提供自由和安全性，用户可完全控制摄像头，避免后门和恶意软件。它支持多种摄像头，基础功能包括视频和音频流。此外，还支持外部云存储、YouTube和Telegram流媒体、SOCKS5代理、虚拟隧道等功能。另有针对无人机、安全头盔、医疗研究等特殊设备的版本。使用OpenIPC于军事目的不被允许，商业使用需联系项目方。

data.author: skrebbel
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了《Bluey》动画的原创艺术总监Catriona Drummond如何打造该剧的场景和背景。Catriona详细描述了从收集布里斯班的视觉参考资料，到通过风格化建筑、色彩和光线，创建出独特的Heelers家庭世界，以及制定展示视觉风格的“风格圣经”的过程。她将自己在布里斯班的生活经验融入到剧中，捕捉该城市的美好与特色，使《Bluey》的场景既亲切又充满魅力。Catriona在23岁时成为澳大利亚最年轻的动画节目首席艺术总监，她与创作者Joe Brumm密切合作，实现了展示布里斯班之美的共同愿景。

How we built Bluey’s world: tales from original series art director, Catriona Drummond
Catriona walks us through the creation of the beloved cartoon’s scenery and backgrounds, from its dollhouse proportions and subtle doggy details, to its distinctly Brisbanite atmosphere.

Bluey
is one of the best kids TV shows ever made – fact. Part of its overall brilliance is its utterly charming and beautiful scenery, which was designed and established by lead art director on series one (and some of series two), Catriona Drummond. Set in Brisbane, Australia, where Catriona is from, the artist brought not only her creative talents but her intrinsic understanding of the city’s landscape to the show. Here, we republish an excerpt of her Substack series
Creating Bluey: Tales from the Art Director
, in particular the article laying bare her process of designing the show’s backgrounds – from gathering visual reference material of Brisbane, to stylising its architecture, colour and light, while building the shape language and proportions for the Heelers’ world, and creating a “style bible” for the show’s visual universe. Read the rest of the series on Catriona’s Substack, Goodsniff,
here
.
Above

When I was approached by Joe Brumm, the creator of
Bluey
, to be its lead art director in 2017, it wasn’t out of the (excuse the pun) blue. I had graduated in 2014, so was relatively fresh out of university, mostly freelancing in advertising doing 2D animation. Every job I took, I tried to inch closer to what I really wanted to do: work in visual development for animated film and television. Living in Australia, there weren’t a lot of prospects for such things. It always felt a little like I was born at the wrong place at the wrong time to do what I really dreamed of.
I had met Joe at the Melbourne International Animation Festival and had made sure to always keep in contact with him to let him know when I was available for work. As, at the time, Joe wasn’t ‘The Creator of
Bluey’,
but the owner of his own animation company, Studio Joho – one of the few studios in Brisbane doing 2D animation work.
Above
Catriona Drummond: development paintings for Bluey (Copyright © Catriona Drummond, 2025)
We finally ended up back in each other’s orbits in 2017 working on a few different projects at Ludo Studio, a Brisbane production company that had started producing some 2D shows. All the while bubbling away in the background was this little show called
Bluey
that Ludo and Joe were trying to get funding for. Somewhere amongst all this, Joe sent me the pilot he’d made, asking whether I’d be interested in hopping on board as art director. Against all odds, I would be getting to do what I’d always dreamed of. And at 23, as far as I know, I was about to become Australia’s youngest lead art director for an animated show.
Joe kicked off the project with a singular and solidified vision for the show’s art direction. He wanted Bluey’s visuals to be beautiful, and show off our hometown of Brisbane, which we both cared so much about. To be honest it was an easy brief, because every other day in Brisbane the weather was so unbelievably good, the everyday scenery so breathtaking, you never wanted to leave. For locals, it was the little secret we kept to ourselves: that Brisbane was the best city in the world. But in starting work on Bluey, we were really about to blow the lid on that.
The initial design phases of Bluey involved tapping into this beauty, as well as employing many fundamental animation design principles. Here, I’ve put together a step-by-step process of how it was done.
Above
Catriona Drummond: development paintings for Bluey (Copyright © Catriona Drummond, 2025)
Above
Catriona Drummond: development paintings for Bluey (Copyright © Catriona Drummond, 2025)
Above
Catriona Drummond: development paintings for Bluey (Copyright © Catriona Drummond, 2025)
Above
Catriona Drummond: development paintings for Bluey (Copyright © Catriona Drummond, 2025)
Step 1: Reference Gathering
For every visual development project, the first thing I do before I even put pen to paper is gather reference. Both photographs and artistic inspiration. Ideally I’ve got a day or two to sit down and gather everything up, absorb it like a sponge, then synthesise it into the early visual exploration.
For Bluey, I already had an exhaustive library of Queenslander homes from my own collection. Joe wanted that quintessential Q

data.title: KDE Plasma prepares crackdown on focus-stealing window behavior under Wayland
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Wayland通过"XDG Activation"机制有效防止窗口焦点被窃取，解决X11中焦点窃取带来的困扰和安全风险。在Wayland下，应用程序需向合成器请求一次性激活令牌以获取焦点，防止未授权窗口擅自获取焦点。KDE开发者Kai-Uwe Broulik计划在KWin中严格执行此机制，新增"极端"焦点防窃设置，确保窗口仅在拥有有效令牌时才能激活。此举解决了多个问题，如Dolphin文件管理器和KRunner等工具的正确激活。同时，后端改进如DBusRunner的SetActivationToken方法确保了文件打开时焦点的正确处理。这一系列改进来源于KDE对Wayland更严格焦点管理的探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：桌面环境中的焦点窃取问题及其解决方案

不同观点：
• Shank和rollcat认为焦点窃取是一个需要解决的严重问题，尤其是在macOS中。他们主张严格限制应用程序在未经用户明确操作的情况下获取焦点，以避免干扰用户工作流程。
• bjoli指出Gnome桌面环境中也存在类似问题，尤其是右键菜单和拖放操作中的焦点窃取，但这些问题未被足够重视和修复。
• margalabargala希望能够标记那些滥用焦点窃取的应用程序，如Zoom，以便单独处理，而不是全面禁止所有应用程序的焦点窃取行为。
• t_mann将FLOSS软件与商业软件进行对比，认为商业软件通过操纵用户行为以获取利润，而开源软件则更注重用户体验和选择自由。
• jm4对焦点窃取问题是否普遍存在提出质疑，认为在自己的Linux和KDE使用体验中未遇到此问题，显示出对问题普遍性的怀疑。
• pseudocomposer对KDE的实现表示兴趣，并询问其他桌面环境（如macOS、Windows、GNOME、XFCE）是否存在类似问题，显示出对跨平台问题比较的兴趣。
• wkat4242赞赏KDE提供的选择自由，认为用户可以自行配置和关闭不需要的功能，这是KDE的优点之一。
• eviks认为KDE的解决方案仍不够彻底，特别是在处理长时间操作时，仍可能干扰用户当前任务。
• ghusto对有人解决此问题表示欣慰，并提到iPad因其应用无法直接访问屏幕而避免了焦点窃取问题，显示出对移动设备体验的偏好。
• nottorp建议仅允许窗口管理器基于用户操作来改变焦点，而非应用程序自行请求焦点，这是一种更严格的解决方案。
• Klaster_1指出浏览器扩展也常存在焦点窃取问题，尤其是在显示更新日志等不必要信息时，干扰用户体验。
• cadamsdotcom赞赏开源软件在细小但关键的细节上的不断改进，尤其是其可配置性。
• rpgbr提到macOS中特定情况下（如右键菜单操作）会出现焦点丢失的问题，显示出对macOS焦点管理的不满。
• SubiculumCode以讽刺口吻描述了密码输入时焦点被随机窗口窃取的问题，强调了这一问题的潜在安全风险。

补充讨论：
• 焦点窃取问题在不同桌面环境（如macOS、Gnome、KDE）中的具体表现和严重性存在差异。
• 解决方案的多样性，包括严格限制焦点改变、标记滥用应用程序、提供用户配置选项等。
• 焦点窃取问题不仅存在于应用程序主窗口，还包括右键菜单、模态对话框、扩展等其他界面元素。

44784312.article_content:
One of the most
interesting things about Wayland
is how it handles window focus, unlike X11, where focus stealing can be frustrating and even a security risk. Its main advantage is a mechanism that prevents focus stealing. The protocol that plays a role in this is known as "XDG Activation."
Here's how it works: Say you double-click a PDF file in your file manager. The file manager first asks the Wayland compositor for a special, single-use "activation token". This request is tied directly to your click, proving a human wanted this to happen.
The file manager then launches your PDF viewer and hands it the token. The PDF viewer, upon starting, shows this token to the compositor and asks to be activated. The compositor checks if the token is legit and, if so, gives the PDF viewer focus.
If the token is missing, old, or otherwise invalid, the compositor says no. The viewer window will not get focus, and instead, its icon in the taskbar will start flashing to grab your attention.
Flashing icon in the taskbar | Image:
Kai-Uwe Broulik
Kai-Uwe Broulik, a KDE developer, recently wrote about the plan to "switch on KWin’s focus stealing on Wayland at a low level". This means KWin, the window manager for KDE Plasma, will begin enforcing this properly.
Under X11, new or dialog windows can only grab focus if their application was most recently active, a check often based on a timestamp called
_NET_WM_USER_TIME
. It was a flimsy system at best. For example, Kai cited how the prevention logic on X11 would sometimes stop the Adobe Flash Player fullscreen window from showing on top of a YouTube video. On X11, an application could just call
XSetInputFocus
on another app's window, and while KWin would try to undo it, focus did flicker for a moment.
Over on Wayland, things are much better with XDG Activation, but some apps still violate the protocol through improper usage. In situations like that, KWin would, by default, just focus any new window that opened. This is changing.
A new "Extreme" setting for "Focus Stealing Prevention" in the Window Management settings will force KWin to activate a window if and only if it requests activation with a valid token.
Image:
Kai-Uwe Broulik
Using this stricter mode, developers Xaver Hugl and Kai-Uwe Broulik have already fixed a ton of issues, introducing several key changes:
Dolphin no longer discards its activation token when launching a new instance.
KRunner, Kickoff, and other Plasmoid popups now correctly request activation.
LayerShell-Qt now requests activation on show and properly reads the
XDG_ACTIVATION_TOKEN
from the environment.
Allowing privileged clients like Plasma to request tokens correctly.
Ignoring modifier key presses for focus prevention logic, since they are often part of a global shortcut.
The work extends to the backend as well, with the DBusRunner specification now gaining a
SetActivationToken
method that is called just before an action runs. Baloo, the desktop search runner, now uses this to ensure that opening files in an existing application window works correctly.
You can learn more on
Kai's blog post.

44784312.article_summary: Wayland通过"XDG Activation"机制有效防止窗口焦点被窃取，解决X11中焦点窃取带来的困扰和安全风险。在Wayland下，应用程序需向合成器请求一次性激活令牌以获取焦点，防止未授权窗口擅自获取焦点。KDE开发者Kai-Uwe Broulik计划在KWin中严格执行此机制，新增"极端"焦点防窃设置，确保窗口仅在拥有有效令牌时才能激活。此举解决了多个问题，如Dolphin文件管理器和KRunner等工具的正确激活。同时，后端改进如DBusRunner的SetActivationToken方法确保了文件打开时焦点的正确处理。这一系列改进来源于KDE对Wayland更严格焦点管理的探索。

data.title: Facts will not save you – AI, history and Soviet sci-fi
data.author: veqq
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人工智能（特别是大型语言模型LLM）在历史叙述、翻译和内容创作中的作用与局限

不同观点：
• munificent认为，由于历史叙述本质上是基于选择性事实和主观信念的重构，LLM无法胜任这项工作。科技公司试图用LLM取代这些工作以控制叙事，从而影响世界。
• dale_glass指出，AI的真正风险在于让我们误以为不需要历史学家或翻译人员。这些领域依赖大量日常工作维持，而AI可能消除这些工作，导致领域萎缩，类似于摄影行业从模拟向数字转变时的困境。
• stereolambda提到，许多历史文献并未数字化或在互联网上公开，LLM无法解决这一基础设施问题。同时，历史叙述往往忽略了大部分事实，仅关注某些主要国家的叙事。
• derbOac认同历史叙述中无法做到完全客观，但一些故事和理论经过更严谨的论证和辩护，具有更高的可信度。
• tombert对微软关于AI取代开发人员的说法持怀疑态度，认为展示AI完成简单任务并不足以证明其能处理复杂、长期的项目，并质疑企业宣传AI能力的动机。

补充讨论：
• ping00分享了一篇短篇小说的阅读体验，并询问其他读者推荐的类似风格作品，这与主讨论点稍有偏离。
• fpoling提供了翻译中文化背景缺失的实例，强调人类翻译在理解和传达背景信息方面的重要性。
• pavel_lishin通过个人经历说明翻译中文化背景和语言细微差别的复杂性，指出即使是人类翻译也常有错误，AI在这方面更具挑战。
• Phui3ferubus和Obscurity4340认同翻译工作正被AI取代，因为企业更注重成本而非质量。

争议焦点：
• AI是否能真正替代需要复杂背景知识和主观判断的工作（如历史叙述和高质量翻译）。
• 企业对AI能力的过度宣传及其潜在动机。
• AI对某些职业（如历史学家、翻译人员、开发人员）的实际影响和替代程度。

data.title: I asked four former friends why we stopped speaking (2023)
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在28岁时对友谊的反思和困惑。作者与最亲密的朋友Simone因生活变化而逐渐疏远，同时在搬到肯尼亚后，也难以融入当地社交圈，感到孤独和不安。作者试图通过与过去的朋友对话，了解友谊破裂的原因，但大部分人无法理解她的困境。文章探讨了人在20多岁时因生活转变、恋爱关系和优先级变化而失去朋友的普遍现象，并表达了缺乏友谊的孤独感和对自我价值的怀疑。作者最终决定通过直接对话 former friends，寻找答案和解决办法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：朋友关系的演变与维持

不同观点：
• TrackerFF认为，朋友关系会随着人生阶段和责任的变化而改变。年轻时由于共同兴趣和环境结交的朋友，可能会因为生活变化（如工作、家庭）而渐行渐远，但随着孩子长大和生活稳定，可能会重新建立联系。
• netsharc幽默地提出了一种应用创意，通过类似"Tinder"的方式来重新连接过去的朋友，但也提到如果没有匹配成功，可以连接心理健康顾问。
• axelpacheco表示，有些朋友即使很久不联系，也不意味着友谊的终结，但意识到这一点可能促使人思考是否需要采取行动。
• avereveard对文章缺乏结论感到不满，并列出了影响友谊持续的因素，如生活转变、缺乏相互努力、价值观分歧等。
• 202508042147分享了与高中朋友断联的经历，认为不再享受彼此的交流时，断开联系反而是一种解脱。
• windowshopping提供了保持友谊的实用建议，包括保持定期沟通、关心对方的生活、适应对方的沟通方式、处理好与对方伴侣的关系、以及创造共同经历。
• silisili引用Matt的故事，强调在20多岁时忙于建立事业和家庭，可能忽略朋友，但随着年龄增长，朋友和亲人变得更加重要。
• programmertote认为，失去与老朋友的联系是生活的一部分，不必感到内疚，人会随着成长而改变，如果缘分到了，可能会再次相遇。
• mmmlinux简短指出，人会改变，环境也会改变，如搬到其他国家。
• ferguess_k描述了因家庭生活而与老朋友渐行渐远，但通过节假日仍保持联系，同时也结交了新朋友。
• malshe感谢Whatsapp帮助保持与老朋友的联系，并在旅行时主动联系。
• jeffhwang赞赏文章作者的坦诚，认为重新连接朋友或公开讨论断联是很难的事情。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是朋友关系的自然演变与人为维持之间的平衡。一些人认为朋友关系会自然变化，不必强求，而另一些人则强调通过努力可以维持友谊。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，技术（如Whatsapp）在维持友谊中的作用，以及如何利用技术有效地保持联系。
• 最后，如何处理与朋友伴侣的关系也被提及，作为维持友谊的一个重要因素。

On a warm July evening, I dove into bed and grabbed my phone, giddy and anxious. As I scrolled through TikTok, attempting to calm my nerves, a Google Calendar notification flashed on the screen: “VIDEO CALL WITH SIMONE.”
Before I could swipe the reminder away, Simone FaceTimed me. I attempted to rehearse my greeting as the call buffered:
Should I keep it cool with a, “Hey, what’s good?” No, that sounds cold. What about a Keke Palmer-esque, “Girl!” No, that’s doing too much. “Good evening?” No, it’s not evening her time, that doesn’t even make sen—
“Girl!” Simone said with a chuckle.
I couldn’t help but crack a smile. As I’d learned over the course of our six-year friendship, her warmth never failed to replace my anxiety with joy.
“Damn, it’s been a
minute
.” she added.
She was right. Though Simone is my closest friend, we don’t see or talk to each other often. Both are my fault. In 2020, after months holed up in my tiny Washington, D.C. apartment, I decided to wait out the winter at my mother’s cottage in Kenya. It was just what the doctor ordered, and a few months later, I decided to move to Nairobi permanently.
My move changed our friendship—it changed
all
of my friendships, actually. I tried to stay in touch with my friends stateside for a while, but as time went on, FaceTime dates became harder to plan, and fewer voice notes were exchanged via WhatsApp. Now, I don’t know if I can call any of them friends anymore—and my relationship with Simone felt like it was hanging by a thread.
Things in Kenya aren’t much better. Though I’m Kenyan by ethnicity, I grew up abroad, in the US and UK, and I’ve found that my foreign accent and perspective other me, even within my family. These days, my social life tends to begin and end with nights on the couch, re-watching
Shameless
with my boyfriend. I’m ashamed and terrified about that reality; it feels dangerous to rely on only him for human connection.
After all, friends are witnesses to your life. They enrich the living experience. Not having that makes me feel like that tree that falls in the forest alone: Can anybody hear me? Do I matter?
Marriage and family therapist Shontel Cargill promises me that these feelings are normal. She says that friendship loss in one’s mid-to-late 20s is common for several reasons: life transitions, romantic relationships, evolution of priorities, and more. And while it doesn’t happen to everyone, for some, friendship loss “can lead to psychological distress,” sparking issues with anxiety, depression, trust, and self-esteem.
Check, check, check, and check.
Cargill says that talking about your struggles with others can help the healing process, but I’ll be honest—that hasn’t worked for me. Most people I’ve spoken to about my predicament don’t get it, which only makes me feel worse. I tried to bring it up on my aforementioned call with Simone, but her empathetic smile and pitying eyes said it all: She couldn’t relate. Lucky her.
I needed answers. Concrete ones—not those generic suggestions that I “put myself out there” or “just give it time.” Everyone around me had managed to hold on to friends throughout their lives; everyone seemed to be on girls’ trips and boozy brunches; seemed to have a tribe of confidants ready to drop everything for them. And here I was, a lonely, overworked 28-year-old who spent way too much time in her apartment, wondering why she didn’t have any of that.
So, like a good journalist, I decided to investigate. After speaking to Simone, I determined that I’d reach out to some of my former friends directly, and see if we could have a conversation about why we “broke up.” Many declined, and understandably so. But to my surprise, a few agreed to participate in my crazy scheme.
Here are those conversations—and their revelations. Their names have been changed.
Celine
Circumstance brought Celine and me together. We were both new freshmen at an international school in Nairobi, and our shared fear proved the perfect BFF elixir. Celine was sweet and reserved, with a quiet confidence that I admired—even more so when I got older. But she wanted to do her own thing and I, a not-so-confident 14-year-old, wanted to fit in. I had a hunger for popularity, and when I realized that Celine didn’t share that, I neglected the friendship. Soon, it evaporated.
Celine remembered things similarly.
“Once school started, we new kids were initially welcomed into the group of ‘misfits’ that every high school has,” she wrote to me via Facebook. “But eventually, we broke away—you, to join the funny kids, a group of hilarious and friendly people who could match your unparalleled wit and high-octane energy and me, to join the kids at the back of the bus, literally and figuratively.”
I thought that by the end of high school, we were strangers. But Celine reminded me that we had our special moments, and that there was always love between the two of us. “By senior year, we were moving in completel

• programmertote认为，失去与老朋友的联系是生活的一部分，不必感到内疚，人会随着成长而改变，如果缘分到了，可能会再次相遇。
• mmmlinux简短指出，人会改变，环境也会改变，如搬到其他国家。
• ferguess_k描述了因家庭生活而与老朋友渐行渐远，但通过节假日仍保持联系，同时也结交了新朋友。
• malshe感谢Whatsapp帮助保持与老朋友的联系，并在旅行时主动联系。
• jeffhwang赞赏文章作者的坦诚，认为重新连接朋友或公开讨论断联是很难的事情。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是朋友关系的自然演变与人为维持之间的平衡。一些人认为朋友关系会自然变化，不必强求，而另一些人则强调通过努力可以维持友谊。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是，技术（如Whatsapp）在维持友谊中的作用，以及如何利用技术有效地保持联系。
• 最后，如何处理与朋友伴侣的关系也被提及，作为维持友谊的一个重要因素。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频编辑器的功能、设计目标及用户需求

不同观点：
• Uehreka认为，要信任一个视频编辑器，必须展示其处理复杂项目的能力，例如30分钟时间线、多段1080p视频文件、每个轨道至少一个效果。他强调即使对初学者而言，编辑器也需要具备处理大文件和不良编辑习惯的能力，而不是仅针对初学者简化功能。他还建议不要从头开始构建编辑器，而应借鉴Cursor的成功经验，利用现有UX和插件生态。

• vivzkestrel提出了一种创新的想法，希望有语音控制或手势控制的视频编辑器，完全摆脱鼠标和键盘操作。这种方法虽然新颖，但目前市场上似乎没有此类产品，可能因为技术实现难度较大。

• Mr_Eri_Atlov对编辑器的简单使用体验表示满意，但提出增加图像居中功能的需求，以改善不同尺寸图像的处理。

• ojr认为市场上已有许多类似视频编辑器，主张开发移动端优先的视频编辑器，而非网页版，并指出需要与Capcut等现有免费桌面应用竞争。

• xnx和microflash则关注该编辑器与其他类似应用（如Omniclip和OpenCut）的比较，希望了解其独特优势。

• sitkack建议预先填充进行中的编辑时间线，让用户可以直接上手体验。

• leptons对编辑器中即将推出的AI功能持怀疑态度，认为AI并非必要，可能分散开发者对核心目标的注意力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于视频编辑器的设计目标，一部分人认为应专注于复杂项目处理能力（Uehreka），另一部分人则希望看到创新功能（vivzkestrel）。
• 对AI功能的必要性存在分歧，leptons认为AI可能分散注意力，而其他评论未直接涉及此功能。
• 市场竞争和平台选择（网页端 vs 移动端）也是讨论的重要方面，ojr特别强调移动端的重要性。

主要讨论点：用户对数学游戏应用的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• **游戏生成问题的准确性存在争议**：
  - [ComplexSystems] 指出"找出异类"游戏中生成的数字有问题，因为答案14被认为不是7的倍数，而其他数字是。此外，"质数游戏"中生成的数字全是合数。
  - [getnormality] 也提到"质数猎人"游戏有时生成的数字集中不包含质数。

• **用户对游戏界面的建议**：
  - [ArekDymalski] 建议为每个游戏提供直接的URL链接，以便分享和让孩子直接玩特定的 puzzle。
  - [seidleroni] 表示希望添加更多基础游戏，适合6岁和8岁孩子。
  - [fsckboy] 提到在点击质数游戏时，界面体验不佳，数字会移出视野，且对数字1是否为质数没有明确说明。此外，Firefox浏览器显示问题导致游戏体验差。

• **游戏设计与玩法建议**：
  - [giantg2] 提出添加一个猜数字游戏（1-100范围内猜7次），通过每次猜中间值来缩小范围，有助于孩子学习结构化解决问题的方法。
  - [AzironaZack] 发现数学网格游戏只需点击增减按钮即可完成，不需要实际计算。

• **关于屏幕时间和竞争的讨论**：
  - [dskhatri] 提到孩子屏幕时间有限，存在许多竞争应用。尽管如此，仍认为该应用界面简单无广告，适合孩子使用。还提到尽管数字书籍功能更多，但物理书籍销量更好，建议开发者考虑出版实体书籍。

• **其他用户反馈与技术问题**：
  - [jacobmarble] 提到Firefox浏览器无法加载页面，出现SSL连接错误。
  - [jamoner] 反馈和问题游戏中的和游戏没有三个数字能加成15。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了自己的类似经验或替代方案：
  - [2kblater] 分享了自己为孩子制作的类似游戏。
  - [nurettin] 提到以前使用过类似教育应用GCompris，现在可以在安卓和F-Droid上使用。

• 用户[pizzathyme] 询问开发者孩子的年龄以及他们是否喜欢这些游戏，但未得到具体回答。

data.author: rob

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新英格兰地区的石墙历史、石墙地图的应用和准确性

不同观点：
• [PyWoody] 指出新英格兰地区的石墙并非如神话所说由霜冻推石而成，而是在大约三十年时间内因养羊业而由人工建造。他引用了Tom Wessels的视频系列来支持这一论点。
• [mikeocool] 补充说明了新英格兰地区石墙的形成背景，由于当地多岩石的土壤，农民将田里的石头移到一旁形成石墙。随着农业的重要性下降和土地的重新造林，这些石墙被遗留下来。

补充讨论：
• [rob] 提供了一个在康涅狄格州查找石墙的LiDAR地图链接，并推荐了具体使用的选项，为实际查找石墙提供了工具。
• [uptime] 提到一些石墙位于百年以前的道路遗迹上，现在这些地方已经被森林覆盖，强调了石墙的历史性和自然环境的变迁。
• [flipnotyk] 从专业角度评论了LiDAR地图的精度，提到其在GIS项目中对数据精确度的要求，对地图的准确性表示赞赏。
• [joshuamcginnis] 提出了对石墙地图实际用途的疑问，引发了对该信息应用价值的讨论。
• [lemonberry] 对地图上街道名称的错误提出了意见，但也确认了地图上一些石墙的准确性。
• [jppope] 从个人兴趣角度出发，表示对石匠技艺的兴趣，认为该地图对学习石工技艺很有帮助。

争议焦点：
• 石墙形成原因的误解与真实历史之间的对比。PyWoody和mikeocool都反驳了关于石墙形成的常见误解，并提供了历史背景和证据支持。

data.title: DrawAFish.com Postmortem
data.author: hallak
data.article_summary: DrawAFish.com 网站经历了一次约6小时的安全事件，期间用户名被恶意篡改为侮辱性词汇，不当的鱼图被批准，正常的鱼图被删除。根本原因包括：遗留的6位管理员密码在过去的数据泄露中被曝光，用户名更新API缺乏身份验证，以及JWT未绑定到特定用户。事件发生后，通过手动恢复管理操作、修复授权逻辑并审查备份来解决问题。此次事件源于作者的快速开发（“vibe-coding”）和多个安全漏洞，如暴露的旧密码和未认证的API。最终，在社区帮助下，问题得以解决，作者从中吸取了教训，强调了高速度开发中的风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个低风险项目“vibe-coded”鱼类展示的评论，涉及安全问题、项目趣味性以及技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ofjcihen] 认为该项目展示了明显的安全漏洞，但因为项目风险低，觉得其文档记录完整，具有一定的幽默感。同时提到，在处理生产环境中类似问题时，自己的工作负载有所增加。
• [vicdemydov1] 对项目的文档记录表示赞赏，并提到该项目与乐高“建造鱼类”展览的相似性，认为这种互动体验具有成瘾性。
• [amiga386] 以讽刺的口吻指出“vibe-coded”中的“S”应代表“安全”，暗示项目在安全方面的不足。
• [Havoc] 提到有人利用安全漏洞来反击恶意行为，认为这种情况很疯狂。
• [somethingawful2] 担心在热门网站上排名靠前会导致个人信息被曝光（doxxing），并询问这种情况是否常见。
• [dmje] 赞赏项目的写作风格和幽默感，并表示希望看到更多类似内容。
• [davikr] 指出项目中JWT（JSON Web Token）认证机制的问题，即未验证JWT与用户身份的关联性，导致潜在的安全风险。
• [thehamkercat] 提到任何人都可以无需认证给鱼类投票，且每分钟每IP地址限制为20票，指出项目在投票机制上的技术细节。
• [lawlessone] 从用户体验角度建议添加镜像功能，以便更容易绘制面向右的鱼。
• [kergonath] 对项目的趣味性表示赞赏，同时提到希望看到有关破坏行为的截图。
• [comrade1234] 分享了在苏黎世发生的类似破坏行为事件，提到在一幅恐龙壁画上出现不雅涂鸦，引发公众笑声。
• [nullc] 引用经典语句“So long and thanks for all the fish”，表达对项目的赞赏。
• [bmau5] 表示项目非常有趣，希望看到更多类似项目。
• [jmull] 讨论了快速编码和代码审查的重要性，质疑使用LLM（大型语言模型）生成代码的合适性，并引用原作者的观点，即LLM是工具，需要人工审查。
• [ofrzeta] 提到有人可能正在研究让LLM自动提交代码，并对“黑客”如何关联到neopets.com用户账户表示好奇。

补充讨论：
• 项目中的安全问题成为讨论焦点，特别是JWT认证机制的漏洞和投票机制的无需认证问题。
• 项目趣味性和互动体验受到多数评论者的赞赏，但也有人提到破坏行为和不雅涂鸦等负面影响。
• 对LLM生成代码的讨论涉及到代码审查的必要性和快速编码的吸引力。

争议焦点：
• 项目中的安全漏洞和如何有效防范恶意行为是主要争议点。
• 对LLM生成代码的适用性和人工审查的重要性存在不同看法。

44784743.article_content:
DrawAFish.com
TL;DR:
Incident Duration:
~6 hours (2AM–8AM EST)
Impact:
Username vandalism (slurs)
Offensive fish approved / safe fish removed
Root Causes:
Legacy 6-digit admin password exposed in past data breach
Username update API lacked authentication
JWT not tied to specific user
Mitigation:
Manual reversal of mod actions, fixed authorization logic, backups reviewed
Takeaway:
hwoopsy daisy 🙂
Did you see? Did you see it? What it says? What it says on top of the website?
If you were on HackerNews on
Aug 1 2025
, you may have seen
DrawAFish.com
.
Because it was in the number 1 spot. You also may have seen it if you follow me on
instagram
. You also probably saw
that I was in the #1 spot on Hackernews there too. Because I posted about it a lot. And also if you
talked to me in person you probably heard about it. And then you probably heard a lot of quotes from
The Social Network
(2010) where I replaced various words with "Fish."
"A million fish isn't cool. You know what's cool?
A billion fish
."
If you read the post on Hackernews, you saw that the website was an exercise in
vibe-coding. I used Copilot to implement features, and I used it to implement features
fast
.
In my career,
[0]
I have learned the art of "Blameless
Postmortems." The problem with a Blameless
Postmortem is that it doesn't really work when you're the sole contributor. So this is a blameful
postmortem. And I blame me. (Not the LLM, sorry).
If you saw the website only on August 1, you probably do not understand why I need to write a postmortem
at
all. Everything went swimmingly (ha, ha). But if you had the displeasure of viewing my website between
the hours of 2AM (20 minutes after I went to sleep) and 8AM (when I woke up)
[1]
EST on Aug 3, then you would have seen chaos. Every single username was
transformed to a heinous slur, many unsavory fish had made it into the fishtank, and many beautiful fish
were gone. How did this happen?
The Vulnerabilities
This is not what they changed my username to. I'll let you use your
imagination.
Legacy admin password exposed in data breach:
When creating the website, I used
my childhood username and my childhood 6-digit password for testing. I think the first time it
leaked was on Neopets.com.
[2]
I then set up
Google Auth. From then on, I only logged in with Google Auth. But the password remained. I
simply forgot. This allowed some of the most intelligent and brilliant minds on the internet to
find my password on the Neopets data leak paste, log in as an admin, and approve and disapprove
some really disgusting and horrible fish.
On the plus side, the brilliant minds (while attempting to ban every single user) managed to
accidentally ban themselves. So that vulnerability was only an active issue for an hour or so.
Username update API lacked authentication:
I vibe coded the profile backend,
which allows users to modify their username. I added this feature last minute, figured I'd
review it later, and then didn't. The username modification did not perform any auth logic
whatsoever. whoopsy
JWT not tied to specific user:
There was another security vulnerability - I
used the JWT to authorize login, but never confirmed that the JWT token belonged to the userId /
email associated with it in the admin actions. So you could log in with my username and password,
grab the JWT, and then send that along with your request. While this was a mistake, it ended up
saving me. Fortunately, hackernews user @
iceweaselfan44
used this vulnerability to authorize as an admin and
delete the really bad fish. He was awake, on the other side of the world, removing fish and
helping out.
[3]
The Recovery
Moderation logs. There are so many of these.
I woke up at around 7:45 am, saw a couple pings and messages, and immediately rushed to my desktop.
[4]
Fortunately, I had set up firebase backups.
Unfortunately, I had set them up wrong. I spent a good hour or so diagnosing the errors and then quickly
pushed changes to require authentication.
I had a mod log set up, so undoing the changes was as simple as writing an annoying script that just
undid all the mod actions. Did I learn my lesson about vibe coding? Maybe. I vibe coded the script,
looked over the code, and did a dry run first.
I banned the other mod account ran by IceWeasel
[5]
and
patched the JWT bug - at which point he reached out to me and explained how he created it. We then
hopped on a call and he took a look at the codebase, where he expertly suggested a refactor that would
be more idiomatic with current security practices. And then when I blindly pushed it and it broke
everything, he expertly committed some more changes that fixed it.
Reflection
At this point, you're probably thinking: geeze man. Wow. youve gotta be stupid.
And I'd like to get on my hands and knees and beg for your suspension of belief when I say: yes I am but
not when it comes to my job. It is really fun to just have high velocity, and it is really fun to not do
code reviews and to just push stuff. Sometime
44784743.article_summary: DrawAFish.com 网站经历了一次约6小时的安全事件，期间用户名被恶意篡改为侮辱性词汇，不当的鱼图被批准，正常的鱼图被删除。根本原因包括：遗留的6位管理员密码在过去的数据泄露中被曝光，用户名更新API缺乏身份验证，以及JWT未绑定到特定用户。事件发生后，通过手动恢复管理操作、修复授权逻辑并审查备份来解决问题。此次事件源于作者的快速开发（“vibe-coding”）和多个安全漏洞，如暴露的旧密码和未认证的API。最终，在社区帮助下，问题得以解决，作者从中吸取了教训，强调了高速度开发中的风险。

data.title: Customizing tmux
data.author: EPendragon
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了终端复用工具 **tmux** 的功能和使用体验。tmux 允许在一个终端中运行多个终端会话，支持创建多个窗口和窗格，便于同时处理多个任务。其主要功能包括保护远程服务器上的运行程序、从不同设备访问远程会话以及灵活的会话管理（如分离和重连）。尽管初始界面不友好且快捷键复杂，但 tmux 高度可定制，用户可以通过编辑 `.tmux.conf` 文件自定义快捷键和外观。例如，更改默认前缀键 `C-b` 为 `C-a`，以及设置分屏和切换窗格的快捷键。文章还提到使用 **iTerm2**、**Powerline10k** 和 **NerdFonts** 可以增强 tmux 的视觉效果。总体而言，tmux 功能强大，但需要一定的学习成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tmux的定制与使用体验

不同观点：
• **保持默认配置 vs 深度定制**：
  - **mrweasel**：倾向于不做过多定制，认为默认配置能在不同服务器间保持一致性，避免远程登录时因不同快捷键配置引发混乱。
  - **lemonwaterlime**：支持深度定制，通过移除不必要的绑定并只设置自己常用的快捷键，减少误操作，使工具更符合个人工作流。

• **Tmux的必要性与替代工具**：
  - **christophilus**：认为自己的窗口管理器已经提供了类似功能，没必要额外学习Tmux的快捷键，仅在需要管理远程服务器时使用。
  - **benrutter**：推荐Zellij作为Tmux的替代品，认为它开箱即用，适合不想做太多定制的人。
  - **AceJohnny2**：推荐Mac用户使用iTerm2，其Tmux集成可以避免使用复杂的快捷键组合，提供更好的用户体验。

• **Tmux的UI和定制体验**：
  - **akkartik**：最初认为Tmux的默认UI不友好，且学习曲线陡峭，但通过定制改善了使用体验，认为定制并非颠覆性改变。
  - **EPendragon**：强调定制Tmux是为了使其更易用和舒适，而非仅仅讨论所有定制选项。
  - **glaucon**：质疑从界面不直观到"gatekeepy"的推论，认为工具难用不一定是有意排除新用户。

• **Tmux在服务器管理中的应用**：
  - **d4rkp4ttern**：利用Tmux的脚本功能，结合Claude-Code工具实现CLI交互，扩展了Tmux的应用场景。
  - **mikepurvis**：关注Tmux作为服务器环境中的进程管理/仪表盘的应用，讨论其与更传统的进程管理工具如systemd的对比，以及可能面临的挑战。

补充讨论：
• **快捷键和前缀键的设置**：
  - **hnarn**：习惯使用默认快捷键，仅在特定情况下做简单定制。
  - **triyambakam**：多年前设置了一个单独的leader键，个人认为非常方便。
  - **d4rkp4ttern**：使用UHK键盘，设置mod-space作为前缀键，非常符合人体工学。

• **其他工具推荐**：
  - **sjbr**：推荐Oh my tmux!，作为Tmux配置的现成解决方案。
  - **Jedd**：推荐byobu作为Tmux的包装，认为它可能更接近某些用户的需求。

争议焦点：Tmux的默认配置是否足够好用，以及深度定制的必要性和价值。

44787374.article_content:
I have been exploring some new tools here and there. When I started watching
Primeagen
, I took a note of several tools that he was using and advocating for. One of them was tmux.
What is tmux?
#
tmux
is a terminal multiplexer. What that means is you can have many terminals in one. According to tmux wiki:
tmux is a program which runs in a terminal and allows multiple other terminal programs to be run inside it. Each program inside tmux gets its own terminal managed by tmux, which can be accessed from the single terminal where tmux is running - this called multiplexing and tmux is a terminal multiplexer.
tmux goes further by allowing you to have a lot of control over how the terminals are displayed, how they function, and how are they styled. You can have many separate windows as tabs. You can have many panes within one window. Are you working on several different projects? Then why don’t you have multiple sessions - each of them containing sets of windows and panes - all giving you access to multiple terminals. With a tool like this you no longer need to arrange multiple terminal instance windows on your desktop or using multiple workspaces for those instances - you can have it all in one place.
One additional feature that tmux boasts in is the ability to retain the terminal session upon its closure. Imagine that you have a long running process like a local server or a persistent connection like ssh session. If you were to close that window, you would lose that session and the process that was in it. Tmux has the ability to detach and attach to multiple sessions making them easier to manage and not to worry about losing it.
tmux wiki goes into detail talking about several other features of tmux:
The main uses of tmux are to:
Protect running programs on a remote server from connection drops by running them inside tmux.
Allow programs running on a remote server to be accessed from multiple different local computers.
Work with multiple programs and shells together in one terminal, a bit like a window manager.
For example:
A user connects to a remote server using ssh(1) from an xterm(1) on their work computer and run several programs. perhaps an editor, a compiler and a few shells.
They work with these programs interactively, perhaps start compiling, then close the xterm(1) with tmux and go home for the day.
They are then able to connect to the same remote server from home, attach to tmux, and continue from where they were previously.
My first tmux experience
#
The first impression of tmux didn’t leave me with much excitement of exploring what is truly possible :/ Source:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Getting-Started
When I first started using tmux, I felt overwhelmed by the very poor default UI that it offers and the amount of options and shortcuts that I needed to know to operate it well and be productive. It took me several tries before I started to feel more or less comfortable with it.
One of the things that stood out to me right away was how dreadful UI looked. Not only it felt uninviting, but it almost felt “gatekeepy” - if you don’t know how to use it in this configuration, then might as well forget about it. But one thing that kept me going was the promise of a highly customizable terminal that I could make my own at some point.
While promising all of these amazing features, the dreadful tmux UI didn’t necessarily inspire :( Source:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Getting-Started
Customization journey
#
To preface, I must mention that I am using
iterm2
with
Powerline10k
and
NerdFonts
. They heavily affect the final look of the tmux due to colors and icons being inherited from the iterm2 configuration. With that said, let’s get into it.
The file that is responsible for customizing tmux - its function and its look - is
.tmux.conf
. This file should be located in user’s Home folder a.k.a.
~/
. That is where tmux will be looking for it.
There are quite a few options when it comes to customizing tmux. One of the first things that I wanted to address was the
prefix
key binding. This prefix is a key combination that you would use to enter the tmux shortcut or command mode. By default, the prefix is
C-b
a.k.a.
Ctrl-b
. One of the common remaps that most people go with is to switch it to
C-a
, which is a lot easier to use. To do that, we need to add the following lines to the configuration file:
# remap prefix from 'C-b' to 'C-a'
unbind C-b
set-option -g prefix C-a
bind-key C-a send-prefix
While researching ways to customize tmux, I stumbled upon several more useful key remaps, which I decided to use:
# split panes using | and -
bind
|
split-window -h
bind
- split-window -v
unbind
'"'
unbind %
# reload config file (change file location to your the tmux.conf you want to use)
bind
r source-file ~/.tmux.conf
;
display-message
"~/.tmux.conf reloaded."
# switch panes using Alt-arrow without prefix
bind
-n M-Left
select
-pane -L
bind
-n M-Right
select
-pane -R
bind
-n M-Up
select
-pane -U
bind
-n M-Down
select

data.title: Show HN: Mathpad – Physical keypad for typing math symbols
data.author: MagneLauritzen
data.article_summary: Mathpad是一款专为简化数学符号输入而设计的键盘，解决了输入数学符号繁琐的问题。它配备了120个数学符号和希腊字母，支持LaTeX、Microsoft Office和LibreOffice等多种输出格式，适用于Windows、macOS和Linux系统。Mathpad采用Gateron KS-33热插拔机械开关，整个设备开源且可定制。项目已完成开发，正在众筹中，计划在活动结束后开始生产并交付。需要注意的是，它仅支持拉丁字母键盘布局，且在Windows系统上需要运行一个小应用程序。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数学符号输入工具（如Mathpad）的实用性、设计和替代方案

不同观点：
• burnt-resistor认为Mathpad类似于缩小版的空间键盘，设计上使用3个修饰键提供了8种模式，但只用了12个键和2个未说明用途的模式，质疑为何不增加更多键和模式。同时提到怀念像HP 48那样便于输入数学符号的设备。

• RossBencina对Mathpad的设计表示赞赏，但提出理想情况下应无需将手从键盘上移开即可访问所有功能。他强调DIY键盘场景中多层键映射的应用，并建议通过增加拇指按钮选择层来实现更高效的输入，同时指出设计和学习键映射是推广该技术的难点。

• throwaway81523质疑Mathpad的价格，认为只需售卖键帽即可，并指出在TeX中输入不常用符号的主要困难在于记住符号名称，推荐使用像dexify这样的工具或图形菜单、手机应用来辅助。

• eviks指出硬件解决方案与软件搜索一样面临无法快速查找符号的问题，建议通过软件提供可视化的符号"作弊表"，并提出在现有大键盘上进行符号映射可能更直观和高效。

• darthoctopus分享了使用.XCompose文件进行符号输入的经验，认为这是一种有效的中间解决方案，兼顾了硬件键盘和图形符号选择器的优点。

• zokier认为QMK固件中Unicode输入不够稳定，建议通过配置QMK键盘的层来实现相同功能，并指出$140的价格可以购买整个键盘，但肯定了Mathpad键帽的精致。

• staplung对Mathpad表示赞赏，并询问如何通过修饰键输入希腊字母的大写形式，如使用shift键加δ来输入∆。

• toomuchtodo对Mathpad表示支持，建议考虑使用Elgato Stream Deck这样的可编程控制面板作为替代方案。

• westurner质疑Mathpad相对于创建包含符号Unicode和LaTeX值的文档表格并通过复制粘贴记忆输入序列的效率提升。

• tonetegeatinst对Mathpad项目表示赞赏，并表示在需要更多LaTeX笔记时会考虑购买。

• olejorgenb对Mathpad的设计表示赞赏，但质疑为何使用交错布局，指出数字键盘并不交错且人们能轻松使用。

What if Mathematical Symbols Were as Easy to Type as Regular Letters?
After 3 years of development, Mathpad finally makes this dream a reality. Anyone who’s struggled to type equations knows the pain: When you need symbols beyond basic arithmetic, you’re forced to hunt for them—copy-pasting from the web, digging through clunky symbol pickers, or memorizing obscure alt-codes. Mathpad fixes this. Just press a key, and the symbol appears instantly.
Works Anywhere You Type
Mathpad is designed to be compatible with nearly every platform and environment where you can type text. Whether you’re writing a lab report in
Microsoft Word
, formatting a paper in
LaTeX
, chatting on
Discord
, or documenting code in
VSCode

Its broad compatibility across

students and professionals

Plaintext symbols for universal communication

LibreOffice Equation Editor codes
Whether you’re a student finishing homework or a researcher publishing your newest work, Mathpad has got your back.
Fully Open Source and Customizable

fully open source
, both hardware and software. Missing a symbol you use daily? No problem! Our
comprehensive documentation
walks you through adding your own symbols - from simple copy-paste customizations to advanced firmware modifications. Mathpad’s firmware is built on

data.title: Every visual workflow tool is just Excel for developers who gave up
data.author: dalibenothmen
data.article_summary: 文章主要批评了视觉工作流工具（如Zapier、Microsoft Power Automate等）实质上是“放弃开发的开发者的Excel”。这些工具看似简化了复杂逻辑的构建，但实际上创造了难以调试的依赖网络，使问题更难解决。作者指出，这些工具的成功并非因为它们更优秀，而是因为开发者变得懒惰和害怕，产生了自我怀疑，并试图避免做大量决策。此外，这些工具通过订阅模式限制用户能力，收取高额费用，使用户在经济和功能上受限。作者呼吁开发者重新审视这些工具的真实价值，并质疑为 inferior 工具付费的合理性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Excel及低代码/无代码工具的优缺点与使用场景

不同观点：
• jdauriemma：认为Excel是一个成功的软件，文章对Excel的批评并不公正。Karen利用Excel创建了一个对公司至关重要的系统，虽然技术债务需要清理，但这是值得的。Excel赋予了非技术人员技术能力，不应贬低。
• taeric：对Excel作为“笔记本式”界面的批评有一定道理，但很多工具实际上是在重新发明 pivot tables。视觉化工具更易于理解，且在沟通上更有效。同时，编程的符号性质对许多人来说是难以理解的。
• Ezhik：支持Excel，认为它是“编码的外行版”。Karen作为会计能够创建一个应用是值得肯定的，不应视为问题。
• throwforfeds：组织选择低代码工具是因为优秀工程师昂贵且难以找到。业务方往往不理解软件开发的复杂性，导致对开发团队施加不合理期望，最终选择低代码工具解决问题。
• skeledrew：认为开发者懒惰但并不害怕新工具，视觉化工具只是软件开发工具进化的下一步。不同开发者对工具的偏好不同，但寻求支持和减少痛苦是选择工具的重要因素。
• daft_pink：Excel的主要问题是不可重用性，虽然是一个不错的工具，但代码在单元格中且与其他单元格紧密耦合，导致难以重用。
• junto：视觉化工作流工具往往被宣传为可以让“高级用户”管理业务流程，但实际上业务用户并不感兴趣，最终还是开发者来处理。视觉化工具难以进行单元测试和版本控制。
• ajcp：认为低代码/无代码平台的价值在于提供管理和安全能力，而不仅仅是用户体验。相比个人Excel工作簿，这些平台提供了更好的可控性和可见性。
• nyeah：建议将编程分为软件开发和较不严肃的自动化劳动，并承认当工具从后者跨入前者时会带来的问题。
• mont_tag：MS Access是一个生产力提升工具，虽然不适用于版本控制，但在其他方面表现出色，特别是可以通过纯文本代码进行扩展。
• wiradikusuma：其开发者同行更倾向于自己开发非视觉化解决方案，而非使用Zapier等视觉工具，但这也带来了一些问题。
• altairprime：企业采用低代码工具是为了降低岗位所需的技能水平，以低技能工人替代高技能程序员，从而增加利润。

补充讨论：
• 视觉化工具在某些领域（如CAD、表单设计）中具有明显优势。

争议焦点：
• Excel及低代码/无代码工具是否真正提升了生产力，还是只是暂时掩盖了技术债务和复杂性。
• 使用低代码/无代码工具是否能替代高技能程序员的工作，以及这种替代是否值得。

A man looking at the window and thinking
Every Visual Workflow Tool is Just Excel for Developers Who Gave Up
Mohamed Ali Ben Othmen
5 min read
·
3 hours ago
--
Listen
Share
There’s a saying that goes “when all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail.” But what happens when you trade your hammer for a Fisher-Price toy hammer and convince yourself it’s an upgrade? That’s exactly what’s happening with visual workflow tools, and I’m tired of pretending it’s not insane.
Every visual workflow tool like Zapier, Microsoft Power Automate, make.com, whatever flavor-of-the-month platform you’re using is just Excel for developers who’ve given up on being developers. And just like Excel, they’re creating a special kind of hell that someone else (probably you, six months from now) will have to deal with.
The Excel Comparison Isn’t an Insult, It’s a Warning
Think about it. Excel and visual workflow tools are fundamentally the same: point-and-click interfaces that let people build complex logic without understanding what they’re actually building. Excel uses cells and formulas, visual workflows use boxes and connectors, but the principle is identical. Both promise to make hard things easy. Both create dependency webs that become absolute nightmares to debug. Both give dangerous amounts of power to people who have no idea what they’re unleashing.
You know what happens with Excel. Karen from accounting builds a “simple” spreadsheet to track expenses. Six months later, it’s a 47-sheet monster with circular references and VLOOKUP formulas that would make a mathematician weep. The company depends on it, nobody understands it, and when it breaks (not if, when), guess who gets called to fix it?
Visual workflows are the same story, just with more colorful boxes and higher monthly fees.
The Question That Should Keep You Up at Night
Here’s what I don’t understand: why are developers whose literal job is to write, understand, and debug code are willingly trading their superpower for drag-and-drop boxes?
Code is infinitely more powerful. You can version control it, test it, refactor it, and when something breaks, you get actual error messages instead of “Node 47 failed.” You can build exactly what you need, scale it however you want, and integrate it with literally anything that has an API.
So why are we choosing tools that are objectively worse at being code? Why are we paying money to make ourselves less capable?
The Uncomfortable Truths We Don’t Want to Admit
Let’s be honest about what’s really happening here. Visual workflow tools aren’t succeeding because they’re better, they’re succeeding because we’ve gotten lazy and scared.
We’ve developed imposter syndrome about our own job.
Somewhere along the way, we started thinking “maybe I’m not smart enough for ‘real’ coding.” So we reach for tools that feel easier, that don’t require us to think through proper architecture or handle edge cases.
We’re suffering from decision fatigue.
Writing code means making a thousand tiny decisions. What framework? How do I structure this? What about error handling? Visual tools reduce those choices, which feels relief until you realize you’ve also reduced your power to actually solve problems.
We’ve bought into the illusion of speed.
“Look, I can build this workflow in 5 minutes!” we say, conveniently ignoring the 5 hours we’ll spend next month trying to figure out why it randomly stopped working.
Management pressure is real.
“Can’t you just use that no-code thing so Sarah from marketing can help maintain it?” Sure, let’s give Sarah the ability to accidentally bring down our entire customer onboarding process. What could go wrong?
But the biggest truth?
We’ve gotten cognitively lazy.
Dragging boxes around feels easier than thinking through the actual problem. It’s the programming equivalent of ordering takeout every night instead of learning to cook.
The Economics Make No Sense
Here’s the part that really gets me: you’re paying premium prices for inferior tools when you literally have the skills to build better solutions for free.
You can write Python, JavaScript, or whatever language you prefer for exactly $0 and have unlimited power. Or you can pay $50+ per month to drag boxes around with artificial constraints. How does this make sense?
These platforms have you trapped in subscription models where you’re paying monthly to be locked into their limited vision of what your workflow should look like. Want to use a custom API? That’s the Enterprise plan for $500/month. Need more than 1000 operations? Upgrade time! Hit a rate limit because too many people are using their shared infrastructure? Sorry, that’s just how it works.
You’re literally paying companies to make you less capable than you naturally are. It’s like a chef paying someone to only let them use a microwave.
The Red Flags You’re Choosing to Ignore
The signs are everywhere, but we keep pretending they’re not deal-breakers:
Vendor lock-in

data.title: 1981 BASIC adventure game comes to a new platform, the TRS-80 MC-10
data.author: vontzy
data.article_summary: 《Arctic Adventure》是一款1981年由Harry McCracken创作的冒险游戏，最初在Radio Shack的TRS-80平台上发布，并收录于《Captain 80's Book of BASIC Adventures》一书中。由于游戏存在严重bug且被遗忘，McCracken在40年后对其进行了修复和改进，使其能在浏览器中运行。游戏修复后获得广泛关注，之后被Jim Gerrie移植到TRS-80 MC-10平台。MC-10是Radio Shack于1983年推出的廉价微型计算机，市场寿命短暂，但因其彩色图形功能而在复古技术圈中受到关注。McCracken对游戏的更新和移植使其从被遗忘的角落重获新生。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MC-10电脑的历史、使用体验及其在市场上的失败原因

不同观点：
• **simmons的观点**：从个人经历出发，认为MC-10是其第一台电脑，虽然因内存不足导致无法运行复杂程序（如"out of memory"错误），但仍对其童年有积极影响。他提到自己曾熬夜输入冒险游戏程序，尽管最终因内存不足未能运行。这一评论强调了MC-10的局限性和个人体验。

• **anthk的观点**：从技术角度提出解决方案，建议将旧程序改编为现代平台如Inform6或ZMachine，以适应当前技术环境。这表明他关注的是如何让旧程序在新系统上运行，侧重技术适应性。
